paper_title: ChARM Character-based Act-adaptive Reward Modeling for Advanced   Role-Playing Language Agents
caption_used: The character distribution in RoleplayPref is organized into three primary categories — Virtual Characters, Custom Characters, and Real Characters — with 13 subcategories in the outer ring. Virtual Characters occupy approximately 60% of the distribution and are subdivided into Comic Characters, Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, and Game Characters, with Movie Characters forming the largest virtual subcategory. Real Characters comprise seven subcategories including Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, Actors, and Influencers, with Musicians representing the largest real-character segment. Custom Characters occupy a small portion with no labeled subcategories.

The central circle is divided into three colored segments: Virtual Characters (light blue, approximately 60% of the total), Real Characters (light green, roughly 35–40%), and Custom Characters (light pink, a small sliver, likely under 5%). The outer ring further subdivides Virtual Characters into five categories — Comic Characters, Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, and Game Characters — with Movie Characters appearing as the largest among them based on arc length. Real Characters are subdivided into seven categories — Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, Actors, and Influencers — with Musicians visually occupying the largest segment within this group. Custom Characters are shown as a single unlabeled segment in the center without further subdivision. The chart uses distinct pastel colors for each main category and includes clear text labels for all subcategories along the outer edge, though no numerical percentages are explicitly marked within the segments. The layout suggests a hierarchical structure, with the central circle representing broad categories and the outer ring detailing their components, arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top.
